     or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "node_modules\\@opensearch-project\\opensearch"
     or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "node_modules/@opensearch-project/opensearch")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","node.exe")
     or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Invoke-WebRequest","DownloadString","curl ","wget ","Buffer.from","child_process","eval(","http.get","https.request")

id: 9f0b4d12-8e3a-4ce1-bf12-2c0e1a5f6d7e
description: Detects npm/yarn/pnpm/node spawning a script-host or download utility while installing the GHSA-27f5-xjrr-q9ff @opensearch-project/opensearch package - characteristic of the malicious postinstall lifecycle hook.
references:
    - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-27f5-xjrr-q9ff

tags:

    - attack.t1059.007

logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\node.exe'
            - '\npm.exe'
            - '\yarn.exe'
            - '\pnpm.exe'
            - '\npx.exe'
        ParentCommandLine|contains:
            - '@opensearch-project/opensearch'
    child_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\curl.exe'
            - '\wget.exe'
            - '\certutil.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
            - '\bash.exe'
            - '\sh.exe'
    child_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'Invoke-WebRequest'
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Buffer.from'
            - 'child_process'
            - 'eval('
    condition: parent and (child_image or child_cmd)
level: high
(source:windows.sysmon OR source:linux.auditd) @ParentImage:(*\\node.exe OR *\\npm.exe OR *\\yarn.exe OR *\\pnpm.exe OR */node OR */npm OR */yarn OR */pnpm) @ParentCommandLine:(*@opensearch-project/opensearch* OR *node_modules\\@opensearch-project\\opensearch* OR *node_modules/@opensearch-project/opensearch*) (@Image:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\cmd.exe OR *\\curl.exe OR *\\wget.exe OR *\\certutil.exe OR *\\bitsadmin.exe OR */bash OR */sh OR */curl OR */wget) OR @CommandLine:(*Invoke-WebRequest* OR *DownloadString* OR *Buffer.from* OR *child_process* OR "*eval(*"))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/^(node|npm|yarn|pnpm|npx)\.exe$/i OR regex("/(node|npm|yarn|pnpm|npx)$", field=ParentImageFileName)
| regex("@opensearch-project/opensearch|node_modules[\\\\/]@opensearch-project[\\\\/]opensearch", field=ParentCommandLine)
| (ImageFileName=/\\(powershell|pwsh|cmd|curl|wget|certutil|bitsadmin|bash|sh)\.exe$/i OR regex("(Invoke-WebRequest|DownloadString|Buffer\\.from|child_process|eval\\()", field=CommandLine))

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b") or SHA1 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b") or MD5 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b") or SHA1 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b") or MD5 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

From PDB strings to MaaS: Tracking a commodity BadIIS ecosystem used by Chinese-speaking threat

Cisco Talos
2026-05-19 10 use cases 4 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

Cisco Talos has uncovered a BadIIS variant — identifiable by its embedded "demo.pdb" strings — that functions as commodity malware, likely sold or shared among multiple Chinese-speaking cyber crime groups operating under a malware-as-a-service (MaaS) model for continuous monetization.

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Article-specific behavioural hunt — From PDB strings to MaaS: Tracking a commodity BadIIS ecosystem used by Chinese-
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] BadIIS demo.pdb variant known SHA256 file/process hashes · [LLM] IIS native module DLL drop or applicationHost.config modification by non-IIS process · Service install for persistence — sc.exe / new service registry write · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] BadIIS C2 IP / domain beacon (lee.6686ty.vip, iis.01nmwe.xyz) · [LLM] IIS worker (w3wp.exe) initiating outbound connection to public IP · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] IIS worker (w3wp.exe) writing robots.txt / .php / .js into web root
[LLM] BadIIS demo.pdb variant known SHA256 file/process hashes Installation High
Detects known BadIIS samples from the Talos demo.pdb commodity ecosystem by exact SHA256 hash on file write, image load, or process execution events. High-confidence retroactive sweep across all hosts. Rationale: Uses the 8 SHA256 IOCs published verbatim in the Talos article. Cross-checked against Elastic's BADIIS write-up and Trend Micro's earlier reporting confirming the same family lineage. Hash matching is article-specific and zero-FP if a hit occurs. Cross-checked against: • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/badiis-to-the-bone-new-insights-to-global-seo-poisoning-campaign • https://www.trendmicro.com/en_us/research/25/b/chinese-speaking-group-manipulates-seo-with-badiis.html

[LLM] BadIIS C2 IP / domain beacon (lee.6686ty.vip, iis.01nmwe.xyz) Command & Control High
Detects any host contacting the published BadIIS command-and-control infrastructure: the two domains used for SEO-fraud orchestration plus the five IPs tied to the demo.pdb variant. Pivots across DNS, network-connection, and proxy telemetry. Rationale: Five IPs and two domains (lee.6686ty.vip, iis.01nmwe.xyz) published in the article. These are operational C2 — any contact is a high-fidelity signal. Cross-validated the campaign infrastructure pattern against Trend Micro's Feb-2025 BadIIS write-up which described similar dual-use C2 (one for SEO redirect targets, one for crawler-cloaking content). Cross-checked against: • https://www.trendmicro.com/en_us/research/25/b/chinese-speaking-group-manipulates-seo-with-badiis.html • https://gbhackers.com/iis-servers/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1568

[LLM] IIS worker (w3wp.exe) initiating outbound connection to public IP Command & Control Medium
Hunts for IIS application-pool worker processes (w3wp.exe) making outbound connections to the public internet. Legitimate IIS sites typically serve inbound; sustained outbound HTTP/HTTPS from w3wp.exe to non-RFC1918 destinations is the textbook BadIIS beacon shape — the malicious native IIS module pulls cloaked SEO content and reports back from inside the worker process. Rationale: Article-specific because BadIIS is a *native IIS module* loaded into w3wp.exe — every C2 beacon, every cloaked-content fetch, every SEO-redirect lookup flows out as outbound HTTP from the worker process. Elastic and Trend Micro both describe the module reaching a backend for crawler-decision content, confirming the egress pattern. Cross-checked against: • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/badiis-to-the-bone-new-insights-to-global-seo-poisoning-campaign • https://blog.alphahunt.io/deep-research-badiis-isnt-enough-the-iis-module-http-fingerprints-that-catch-seo-fraud-cloaking/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1090 T1505.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "w3wp.exe"
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where ActionType in ("ConnectionSuccess","ConnectionAttempt","ConnectionRequest")
| where RemotePort in (80, 443, 8080, 8443)
| summarize ConnCount=count(), DistinctDests=dcount(RemoteIP), SampleUrl=any(RemoteUrl), SampleCmd=any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine), FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where ConnCount > 3
| order by ConnCount desc
let IISHosts = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActingProcessName =~ "w3wp.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "\\w3wp.exe"
    | summarize by DvcHostname;
ImNetworkSession

| where DvcHostname in (IISHosts) or SrcHostname in (IISHosts)
| where DstPortNumber in (80, 443, 8080, 8443)
| where DstIpAddr !startswith "10." and DstIpAddr !startswith "192.168." and DstIpAddr !startswith "127." and DstIpAddr !startswith "169.254."
| where not(DstIpAddr matches regex @"^172\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[0-1])\.")
| summarize ConnCount=count(), DistinctDests=dcount(DstIpAddr), SampleHost=any(DstHostname), FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated) by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 3
| order by ConnCount desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 (@Image:(*\\w3wp.exe OR *\\W3wp.exe OR *\\W3WP.EXE)) (@DestinationPort:(80 OR 443 OR 8080 OR 8443)) -CIDR(@DestinationIp, 10.0.0.0/8) -CIDR(@DestinationIp, 172.16.0.0/12) -CIDR(@DestinationIp, 192.168.0.0/16) -CIDR(@DestinationIp, 127.0.0.0/8)

[LLM] IIS native module DLL drop or applicationHost.config modification by non-IIS process Installation High
Detects file writes of DLLs into IIS module load paths (System32\inetsrv, Microsoft.NET\Framework64) or modifications to applicationHost.config performed by processes other than the standard IIS / Windows-installer service set. This is the BadIIS persistence install footprint — the malware copies its DLL into a module path then registers it via globalModules. Rationale: Article describes 'service-based installers, droppers, and persistence mechanisms that automate deployment, ensure survivability across IIS server restarts.' External corroboration (Elastic, Trend Micro) confirms BadIIS persistence is exactly this: DLL copied to inetsrv\ or Microsoft.NET\Framework64\ + applicationHost.config edited to register the module. Filtering out TrustedInstaller / msiexec / mscorsvw / appcmd / IIS-setup binaries leaves the BadIIS installer's footprint exposed. Cross-checked against: • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/badiis-to-the-bone-new-insights-to-global-seo-poisoning-campaign • https://www.welivesecurity.com/2021/08/06/anatomy-native-iis-malware/ • https://www.trendmicro.com/en_us/research/25/b/chinese-speaking-group-manipulates-seo-with-badiis.html
ATT&CKT1505.004 T1543.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where (FolderPath has @"\inetsrv\" and FileName endswith ".dll")
    or (FolderPath has @"\Microsoft.NET\Framework64\" and FileName endswith ".dll")
    or (FolderPath has @"\Microsoft.NET\Framework\" and FileName endswith ".dll")
    or FileName =~ "applicationHost.config"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("TrustedInstaller.exe","msiexec.exe","mscorsvw.exe","iissetup.exe","appcmd.exe","WindowsAdminCenter.exe","WaAppAgent.exe","WindowsAzureGuestAgent.exe","MsDeploy.exe","ngen.exe","setup.exe","trustedinstaller.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
let SuspectFile = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed","Created","Modified")
    | where (TargetFilePath has @"\inetsrv\" and TargetFileName endswith ".dll")
        or (TargetFilePath has @"\Microsoft.NET\Framework64\" and TargetFileName endswith ".dll")
        or (TargetFilePath has @"\Microsoft.NET\Framework\" and TargetFileName endswith ".dll")
        or TargetFileName =~ "applicationHost.config"
    | where ActingProcessName !in~ ("TrustedInstaller.exe","msiexec.exe","mscorsvw.exe","iissetup.exe","appcmd.exe","WindowsAdminCenter.exe","WaAppAgent.exe","WindowsAzureGuestAgent.exe","MsDeploy.exe","ngen.exe","setup.exe")
    | project TimeGenerated, Source="FileEvent", DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256;
let SuspectProcess = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActingProcessName =~ "appcmd.exe"
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("install module","add module","/section:globalModules","/section:modules")
    | project TimeGenerated, Source="ProcessCreate", DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName;
union SuspectFile, SuspectProcess
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: BadIIS Native Module DLL Drop or applicationHost.config Modification
id: c4d8e2a1-6b9f-4d3e-a872-3f1c4e9b7d22
description: Detects file writes of DLLs into IIS module-load paths or modifications to applicationHost.config by processes outside the standard IIS / Windows-installer set — the persistence footprint of BadIIS (Talos demo.pdb variant).

level: high

[LLM] IIS worker (w3wp.exe) writing robots.txt / .php / .js into web root Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects IIS worker process writing or modifying SEO-fraud artifact files (robots.txt, PHP backlink scripts, JavaScript redirectors, hijacked HTML) inside the IIS web-root tree. Legitimate IIS workers serve files; only a malicious in-process module writes content back into wwwroot — the exact SEO-fraud and content-hijacking behaviour the Talos article describes including 'compatible with Baidu browser + hijacking robots.txt' and 'JavaScript redirectors, PHP backlink scripts'. Rationale: Article explicitly calls out 'compatible with Baidu browser + hijacking robots.txt' as a malware feature folder, plus 'JavaScript redirectors, PHP backlink scripts' as the builder's output. w3wp.exe writing into its own wwwroot is the most article-specific behavioural signal — legitimate web apps almost never have the worker process modify static SEO files. Elastic's BADIIS write-up corroborates the cloaking-content delivery path through w3wp.exe. Cross-checked against: • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/badiis-to-the-bone-new-insights-to-global-seo-poisoning-campaign • https://blog.alphahunt.io/deep-research-badiis-isnt-enough-the-iis-module-http-fingerprints-that-catch-seo-fraud-cloaking/
ATT&CKT1505.004 T1565.001 T1608.006
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "w3wp.exe"
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where (FileName =~ "robots.txt")
    or (FolderPath has @"\inetpub\wwwroot\" and (FileName endswith ".php" or FileName endswith ".js" or FileName endswith ".html" or FileName endswith ".htm"))
    or (FolderPath has @"\inetpub\" and FileName =~ "robots.txt")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName =~ "w3wp.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "\\w3wp.exe"
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed","Created","Modified")
| where (TargetFileName =~ "robots.txt")
    or (TargetFilePath has @"\inetpub\wwwroot\" and (TargetFileName endswith ".php" or TargetFileName endswith ".js" or TargetFileName endswith ".html" or TargetFileName endswith ".htm"))
    or (TargetFilePath has @"\inetpub\" and TargetFileName =~ "robots.txt")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic

    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time

| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("143.92.36.109", "38.181.52.147", "154.23.186.99", "154.36.149.4", "45.194.17.133")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("lee.6686ty.vip", "iis.01nmwe.xyz")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("lee.6686ty.vip", "iis.01nmwe.xyz")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("143.92.36.109", "38.181.52.147", "154.23.186.99", "154.36.149.4", "45.194.17.133")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("lee.6686ty.vip", "iis.01nmwe.xyz")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("lee.6686ty.vip", "iis.01nmwe.xyz")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
Service install for persistence — sc.exe / new service registry write Installation High
Service install with binPath pointing to user-writeable path or LOLBin. Detects via process telemetry (sc.exe create) and registry (HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\* writes).
ATT&CKT1543.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Registry DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName =~ "sc.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "create"
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(\Users\|\AppData\|\ProgramData\|\Temp\)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
// EventID 4697 is "Service installed" — direct signal, no cmdline-regex needed.
union
    ( SecurityEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where EventID == 4697
        | where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
        | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account = SubjectUserName,
                  Detail = strcat("ServiceName=", ServiceName, " | Image=", ServiceFileName) ),
    ( SecurityEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where EventID == 4688
        | where Account !endswith "$"
        | where NewProcessName endswith "\sc.exe" and CommandLine has "create"
        | where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(\Users\|\AppData\|\ProgramData\|\Temp\)"
        | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account,
                  Detail = strcat("4688 sc.exe create: ", CommandLine) )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Service Persistence via sc.exe with User-Writable Path
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0e
status: experimental
description: |
    sc.exe create with the binary path under \Users\, \AppData\,
    \ProgramData\, or \Temp\ — service-install persistence outside
    legitimate program directories.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1543/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1543.003
    - attack.persistence
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_sc:
        Image|endswith: '\sc.exe'
        CommandLine|contains: 'create'
    selection_path:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '\Users\'
            - '\AppData\'
            - '\ProgramData\'
            - '\Temp\'
    condition: selection_sc and selection_path
falsepositives:
    - Internal install scripts dropping a service from %ProgramData%
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name="sc.exe" AND Processes.process="*create*"
      AND (Processes.process="*\Users\*" OR Processes.process="*\AppData\*"
        OR Processes.process="*\ProgramData\*" OR Processes.process="*\Temp\*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry
        where Registry.registry_path="*\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\*"
          AND Registry.registry_value_name="ImagePath"
          AND (Registry.registry_value_data="*\Users\*"
            OR Registry.registry_value_data="*\AppData\*"
            OR Registry.registry_value_data="*\Temp\*")
        by Registry.dest, Registry.registry_path, Registry.registry_value_data, Registry.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)`]
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name="sc.exe" AND Processes.process="*create*"
      AND (Processes.process="*\Users\*" OR Processes.process="*\AppData\*"
        OR Processes.process="*\ProgramData\*" OR Processes.process="*\Temp\*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry
        where Registry.registry_path="*\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\*"
          AND Registry.registry_value_name="ImagePath"
          AND (Registry.registry_value_data="*\Users\*"
            OR Registry.registry_value_data="*\AppData\*"
            OR Registry.registry_value_data="*\Temp\*")
        by Registry.dest, Registry.registry_path, Registry.registry_value_data, Registry.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)`]

title: File or Process Matching Article Hash IOCs
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0b
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__HASH_LIST__` placeholder with article-specific SHA256
    values. Use a watchlist or external indicator file for management
    at scale.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Hashes|contains:
            - 'SHA256=__HASH_PLACEHOLDER_REPLACE_ME__'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive hash match
level: critical

Mini Shai-Hulud strikes again: npm worm compromises hundreds of @antv packages

AikidoStepSecurity
2026-05-19 14 use cases 3 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

A new wave of the Mini Shai-Hulud worm has compromised packages across Alibaba's AntV data visualization ecosystem, echarts-for-react, timeago.js, and dozens more. Stolen CI/CD secrets are being dumped to thousands of public GitHub repositories as the attack continues to spread.

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Mini Shai-Hulud strikes again: npm worm compromises hundreds of @antv packages
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud npm worm payload by SHA256 · [LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud persistence hooks written into .vscode/ and .claude/ configs · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud C2 exfil to t.m-kosche.com disguised as OpenTelemetry collector · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] GitHub Actions Runner.Worker process-memory secret scraping via /proc · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
[LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud C2 exfil to t.m-kosche.com disguised as OpenTelemetry collector Command & Control High
Hunts outbound connections/DNS to the campaign's fallback C2 t.m-kosche.com, which receives RSA-encrypted stolen credentials over OpenTelemetry-style paths (/api/public/otel/v1/traces) on 443. The domain is unique to this campaign and confirmed by multiple vendors, making any contact high-fidelity. Rationale: Anchored on the campaign-unique C2 domain t.m-kosche.com confirmed by StepSecurity, Microsoft, Snyk and JFrog write-ups; the OTel path /api/public/otel/v1/traces detail was added from cross-referenced sources. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/shai-hulud-here-we-go-again-mass-npm-supply-chain-attack-hits-the-antv-ecosystem • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/05/20/mini-shai-hulud-compromised-antv-npm-packages-enable-ci-cd-credential-theft/ • https://research.jfrog.com/post/shai-hulud-here-we-go-again-may19/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1041
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has "m-kosche.com"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DnsQuery has "m-kosche.com"
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, DnsQuery, DnsResponseName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud npm worm payload by SHA256 Installation High
Detects the worm's obfuscated payload file landing or executing on a host by its confirmed SHA256 hashes. High-fidelity exact-match IOC for the AntV-wave payload. Rationale: Uses the two pre-extracted SHA256 payload hashes as exact-match file/process IOCs — zero ambiguity, only ships because the campaign is documented by multiple vendors. Cross-checked against: • https://www.snyk.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-antv-npm-supply-chain-attack/ • https://research.jfrog.com/post/shai-hulud-here-we-go-again-may19/

[LLM] GitHub Actions Runner.Worker process-memory secret scraping via /proc Actions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the worm's embedded Python helper that scans /proc for the Runner.Worker process and reads its memory to recover masked CI/CD secrets in plaintext. Targets Linux CI runners where a node/npm-spawned interpreter references Runner.Worker or /proc/<pid>/mem. Rationale: Anchored on the campaign-specific Runner.Worker /proc memory-scraping technique (the novel CI secret-recovery method) corroborated by Microsoft and the Securonix beta analytic; scoped to npm/node-spawned interpreters to cut noise. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/05/20/mini-shai-hulud-compromised-antv-npm-packages-enable-ci-cd-credential-theft/ • https://connect.securonix.com/threat-research-intelligence-62/beta-detection-mini-shai-hulud-runner-worker-memory-secret-extraction-analytic-308
ATT&CKT1003.007 T1552.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has "Runner.Worker" or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/proc/self/mem","process_vm_readv") or ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"/proc/[0-9]+/mem"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","npm","npx","sh","bash","python","python3")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where SyslogMessage has "Runner.Worker" or SyslogMessage has_any ("/proc/self/mem","process_vm_readv")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("node","npm","python")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, ProcessName, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud persistence hooks written into .vscode/ and .claude/ configs Installation Medium
Detects node/npm/npx processes writing into .vscode/ or .claude/ configuration directories, where the worm plants auto-execution hooks that survive across sessions and cloned repos. Combination of a JS toolchain process touching these trusted IDE/agent config dirs is the article-specific signal. Rationale: Anchored on the worm's documented persistence in .claude/ and .vscode/ trusted config dirs (Akamai/Microsoft); scopes to the JS toolchain (node/npm/npx) as the writing process to separate from normal IDE activity. Cross-checked against: • https://www.akamai.com/blog/security-research/mini-shai-hulud-worm-returns-goes-public • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/05/20/mini-shai-hulud-compromised-antv-npm-packages-enable-ci-cd-credential-theft/
ATT&CKT1554 T1546
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FolderPath contains ".vscode" or FolderPath contains ".claude"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node","npm.cmd","npm","npx.cmd","npx")
| where FileName endswith ".json" or FileName endswith ".js" or FileName endswith ".sh"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFilePath has ".vscode" or TargetFilePath has ".claude"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node","npm","npx")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142") or SHA1 in~ ("a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142") or MD5 in~ ("a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142") or SHA1 in~ ("a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142") or MD5 in~ ("a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

actions-cool/issues-helper GitHub Action Compromised: All Tags Point to Imposter Commit That Exfiltrates CI/CD Credentials

StepSecurity
2026-05-19 6 use cases 0 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

The popular GitHub Action actions-cool/issues-helper has been compromised. Every existing tag in the repository has been moved to point to a single imposter commit that does not appear in the action's normal commit history. That commit contains malicious code that exfiltrates credentials from CI/CD pipelines that run the action.

Domainst.m-kosche.com

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] GitHub workflow references actions-cool/issues-helper or maintain-one-comment by tag
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Article-specific behavioural hunt — actions-cool/issues-helper GitHub Action Compromised: All Tags Point to Imposter
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] bun runtime executed on CI runner spawning python3 with sudo escalation
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Outbound C2 to t.m-kosche.com from CI/CD runner or any endpoint · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] python3 reading /proc/<PID>/mem to scrape Runner.Worker secrets
[LLM] Outbound C2 to t.m-kosche.com from CI/CD runner or any endpoint Command & Control High
Hunts the exfiltration callback used by the compromised actions-cool/issues-helper and actions-cool/maintain-one-comment GitHub Actions. Any DNS resolution or HTTPS connection to t.m-kosche.com from a runner, developer workstation, or build agent indicates secrets-in-flight exfiltration. Rationale: Pure-IOC detection on t.m-kosche.com — the attacker-controlled exfil domain named explicitly in the StepSecurity advisory and corroborated by The Hacker News, GBHackers, and SC Media. The domain is on the Harden-Runner global block list. Cross-checked with the StepSecurity X post and the Mini Shai-Hulud cluster note from coverage. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/actions-cool-issues-helper-github-action-compromised-all-tags-point-to-imposter-commit-that-exfiltrates-ci-cd-credentials • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/github-actions-supply-chain-attack.html • https://gbhackers.com/compromised-github-action/ • https://cybersecuritynews.com/compromised-github-action-exfiltrates-workflow-credentials/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1567
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Network_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
let exfil_domain = "m-kosche.com";
union isfuzzy=true
(DeviceNetworkEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where RemoteUrl has exfil_domain or RemoteUrl endswith ".m-kosche.com"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, ActionType),
(DeviceEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where ActionType in ("DnsQueryResponse","ConnectionSuccess")
  | where RemoteUrl has exfil_domain or AdditionalFields has exfil_domain
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, AdditionalFields)
| order by Timestamp desc
let exfil_domain = "m-kosche.com";
union isfuzzy=true
(DnsEvents | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where Name has exfil_domain | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, ServerIPAddress),
(CommonSecurityLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where DestinationHostName has exfil_domain or RequestURL has exfil_domain or DestinationDnsDomain has exfil_domain | project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, SourceUserName),
(ImDnsActivity | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where DnsQuery has exfil_domain | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, DnsQuery, DnsQueryType, DnsResponseName),
(ImWebSession | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where Url has exfil_domain or HttpHostName has exfil_domain | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, Url, HttpHostName, HttpMethod, HttpStatusCode)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

id: 7d3a4e5b-9c1f-4f72-b6a0-6b2f4e9d1c84
status: experimental
description: Detects DNS resolution or HTTPS connection to t.m-kosche.com, the exfiltration domain used by the compromised actions-cool/issues-helper and actions-cool/maintain-one-comment GitHub Actions to receive secrets harvested from Runner.Worker memory.
references:
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/actions-cool-issues-helper-github-action-compromised-all-tags-point-to-imposter-commit-that-exfiltrates-ci-cd-credentials
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/github-actions-supply-chain-attack.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
  - attack.exfiltration
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.t1567
  - attack.command_and_control
logsource:
  category: dns
detection:
  selection:
    QueryName|endswith:
      - 'm-kosche.com'
      - '.m-kosche.com'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - None expected. The domain is attacker-controlled and listed on the Harden-Runner global block list.
level: high
(@dns.question.name:(*m-kosche.com OR *.m-kosche.com) OR @network.destination.name:(*m-kosche.com OR *.m-kosche.com) OR @http.url:(*m-kosche.com* OR *M-KOSCHE.COM*) OR @url.domain:(m-kosche.com OR *.m-kosche.com))
(#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/(^|\.)m-kosche\.com$/i) OR (#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 ContextImageFileName=/(bun|node|python3|curl|wget)/i) | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName, RemoteAddressIP4], function=count()) | sort(field=_count, order=desc)
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(DNS.src) as src values(DNS.query) as query from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where DNS.query="*m-kosche.com" by DNS.src DNS.query | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` | append [| tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.url="*m-kosche.com*" OR Web.dest="*m-kosche.com*" by Web.src Web.dest Web.url | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`] | append [| tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest="*m-kosche.com*" by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`]
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(DNS.src) as src values(DNS.query) as query from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where DNS.query="*m-kosche.com" by DNS.src DNS.query | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` | append [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.url="*m-kosche.com*" OR Web.dest="*m-kosche.com*" by Web.src Web.dest Web.url | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`] | append [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest="*m-kosche.com*" by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`]
[LLM] python3 reading /proc/<PID>/mem to scrape Runner.Worker secrets Actions on Objectives High
Hunts the exact credential-harvesting primitive used by the compromised actions-cool actions: a python3 process opening another process's /proc/<PID>/mem to scrape decrypted GitHub Actions secrets from Runner.Worker memory. The behaviour is rare on legitimate CI/CD runners and developer Linux endpoints. Rationale: Anchors on the exact behaviour the article and StepSecurity Harden-Runner traces describe: python3 reading /proc/<PID>/mem against the Runner.Worker process (PID 2119 in their controlled test) and grep-filtering for `isSecret`:true tokens. Cross-process /proc/<PID>/mem reads by python on Linux are a high-fidelity credential-access signal — this is essentially T1003.007 in script form. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/actions-cool-issues-helper-github-action-compromised-all-tags-point-to-imposter-commit-that-exfiltrates-ci-cd-credentials • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/github-actions-supply-chain-attack.html • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/007/
ATT&CKT1003.007 T1552.001 T1059.006
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName matches regex @"^python3?(\.\d+)?$" or InitiatingProcessFileName matches regex @"^python3?(\.\d+)?$"
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"/proc/\d+/mem"
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("isSecret","Runner.Worker")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"/proc/\d+/mem"
| extend ProcMemTarget = extract(@"/proc/(\d+)/mem", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, ProcMemTarget, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let lookback = 30d;
union isfuzzy=true
(Syslog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
  | where Facility in ("authpriv","auth","daemon","user")
  | where SyslogMessage matches regex @"(?i)python3?[^\s]*\s+[^\n]*/proc/\d+/mem"
     or SyslogMessage has_any ("isSecret","Runner.Worker")
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostIP, ProcessName, SyslogMessage),
(ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
  | where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)python3?(\.\d+)?$"
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"/proc/\d+/mem"
     or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("isSecret","Runner.Worker")
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Python Process Reading /proc/<PID>/mem (CI Runner Memory Scrape)
id: 2b8f1a64-3d97-4d8c-9c0e-1b2af3b6e711
status: experimental
description: Detects a python interpreter executed with a /proc/<PID>/mem path in its command line, the credential-dump primitive used by the compromised actions-cool/issues-helper and actions-cool/maintain-one-comment GitHub Actions to scrape Runner.Worker memory and exfiltrate decrypted secrets tagged "isSecret":true.
references:
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/actions-cool-issues-helper-github-action-compromised-all-tags-point-to-imposter-commit-that-exfiltrates-ci-cd-credentials
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/github-actions-supply-chain-attack.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
  - attack.credential_access
  - attack.t1003.007
  - attack.t1552.001
  - attack.t1059.006
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/python'
      - '/python3'
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|re: '/proc/\d+/mem'
  selection_str:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'isSecret'
      - 'Runner.Worker'
  condition: selection_proc and (selection_cmd or selection_str)
falsepositives:
  - Forensic / memory-acquisition tooling (volatility, lime, avml) operated by IR teams
  - Debugging by developers reading their own process memory for diagnostics
level: high
source:(linux.auditd OR linux.syslog) (@process.executable.path:(*/python3 OR */python OR */python3.* OR */PYTHON3) OR @process.name:(python3 OR python OR PYTHON3)) (@process.command_line:*\/proc\/* AND @process.command_line:*\/mem*) OR @process.command_line:*isSecret* OR @process.command_line:*Runner.Worker*
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\/python3?(\.\d+)?$/i | regex("/proc/\d+/mem|isSecret|Runner\.Worker", field=CommandLine) | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count()) | sort(field=_count, order=desc)
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("python","python3") AND (Processes.process="*/proc/*/mem*" OR Processes.process="*isSecret*" OR Processes.process="*Runner.Worker*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where match(cmdline, "(?i)/proc/\d+/mem") OR match(cmdline, "(?i)isSecret|Runner\.Worker")
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("python","python3") AND (Processes.process="*/proc/*/mem*" OR Processes.process="*isSecret*" OR Processes.process="*Runner.Worker*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where match(cmdline, "(?i)/proc/\d+/mem") OR match(cmdline, "(?i)isSecret|Runner\.Worker")
[LLM] bun runtime executed on CI runner spawning python3 with sudo escalation Installation High
Hunts the install-stage of the actions-cool/issues-helper compromise: the imposter commit's index.js downloads the bun JavaScript runtime onto the runner, which then spawns python3 via sudo to read Runner.Worker memory. The bun→python3→sudo chain is the article's signature behaviour. Rationale: Anchors on the article's verbatim chain: `bun` runtime (which the imposter commit explicitly downloads to the runner) spawning python3, sudo, and `gh auth token`. This combination is essentially unique to the attack — bun is a JS runtime, not a Python wrapper, and bun→sudo is anomalous in any normal CI workflow. Cross-checked against StepSecurity Harden-Runner test run capture (linked in advisory) and confirmed by Hacker News + GBHackers coverage. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/actions-cool-issues-helper-github-action-compromised-all-tags-point-to-imposter-commit-that-exfiltrates-ci-cd-credentials • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/github-actions-supply-chain-attack.html • https://gbhackers.com/compromised-github-action/
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1548.003 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let lookback = 30d;
let BunHosts = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
    | where FileName =~ "bun" or FolderPath endswith "/bun" or ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(curl|wget)[^\n]*bun\.sh"
    | project BunTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, BunPid = ProcessId, BunCmd = ProcessCommandLine, BunParent = InitiatingProcessFileName;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "bun"
| where FileName in~ ("python","python3","sudo","gh")
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("gh auth token","sudo python3","/proc/","isSecret")
| join kind=inner BunHosts on DeviceId
| where Timestamp between (BunTime .. BunTime + 10m)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, BunTime, BunCmd, BunParent, ChildImage = FileName, ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine, ChildSha256 = SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let lookback = 30d;
let BunHosts = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
    | where ActingProcessName endswith "/bun" or ActingProcessName =~ "bun" or ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(curl|wget)[^\n]*bun\.sh"
    | project BunTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, BunPid = ActingProcessId, BunCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine;
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where ParentProcessName endswith "/bun" or ParentProcessName =~ "bun"
| where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)/(python3?|sudo|gh)$"
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("gh auth token","sudo python3","/proc/","isSecret")
| join kind=inner BunHosts on DvcHostname
| where TimeGenerated between (BunTime .. BunTime + 10m)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, BunCmd, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: bun Runtime Spawning python3/sudo/gh-auth-token on Linux (actions-cool Compromise)
id: c8a4b2e1-7d61-4c30-9f12-5e3a1c9b4a07
status: experimental
description: Detects the bun JavaScript runtime executing python3, sudo, or `gh auth token` as a child process — the exact in-runner chain used by the compromised actions-cool/issues-helper and actions-cool/maintain-one-comment GitHub Actions to harvest Runner.Worker secrets.
references:
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/actions-cool-issues-helper-github-action-compromised-all-tags-point-to-imposter-commit-that-exfiltrates-ci-cd-credentials
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/github-actions-supply-chain-attack.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.007
  - attack.t1548.003
  - attack.t1195.002
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  parent_bun:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/bun'
  child_signal:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/python'
      - '/python3'
      - '/sudo'
      - '/gh'
  cmd_signal:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'gh auth token'
      - 'sudo python3'
      - '/proc/'
      - 'isSecret'
  condition: parent_bun and (child_signal or cmd_signal)
falsepositives:
  - bun-native projects that legitimately shell out to python build scripts (rare — most bun projects are pure JS/TS)
  - Developer experimentation on a workstation running both bun and python tooling
level: high
source:(linux.auditd OR linux.syslog) (@process.parent.executable.path:(*/bun OR */BUN) OR @process.parent.name:(bun OR BUN)) AND (@process.name:(python3 OR python OR sudo OR gh) OR @process.command_line:(*"gh auth token"* OR *"sudo python3"* OR *"/proc/"* OR *isSecret*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^bun$/i | regex("/python3?$|/sudo$|/gh$", field=ImageFileName) OR regex("gh auth token|sudo python3|/proc/\d+/mem|isSecret", field=CommandLine) | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count()) | sort(field=_count, order=desc)
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as bun_cmd values(Processes.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name=bun OR Processes.process="*bun*" OR Processes.process="*/bun *") by Processes.dest Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | join type=inner dest [| tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name=bun (Processes.process_name IN ("python","python3","sudo") OR Processes.process="*gh auth token*") by Processes.dest Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | rename process as child_cmd process_name as child_name]
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as bun_cmd values(Processes.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name=bun OR Processes.process="*bun*" OR Processes.process="*/bun *") by Processes.dest Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | join type=inner dest [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name=bun (Processes.process_name IN ("python","python3","sudo") OR Processes.process="*gh auth token*") by Processes.dest Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | rename process as child_cmd process_name as child_name]
[LLM] GitHub workflow references actions-cool/issues-helper or maintain-one-comment by tag Delivery High
Hunts use of the compromised GitHub Actions in any repository referenced by tag (or by a moved-tag SHA) rather than a pinned, audited full commit SHA. Anything other than a pinned SHA on the pre-compromise commit history will pull the imposter commit on next run. Rationale: Pure-IOC supply-chain detection on the two actions named by StepSecurity and corroborated by The Hacker News (`actions-cool/issues-helper` and `actions-cool/maintain-one-comment` — same actor, identical TTP). GitHub disabled the upstream repos, but any pre-existing pinned reference by tag or by a moved-tag SHA in a workflow YAML still resolves to the imposter commit on the next run until the workflow is patched. Detection should fire at workflow-prepare time (GitHub audit logs) and again on any commit/PR that adds such a reference. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/actions-cool-issues-helper-github-action-compromised-all-tags-point-to-imposter-commit-that-exfiltrates-ci-cd-credentials • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/github-actions-supply-chain-attack.html • https://cybersecuritynews.com/compromised-github-action-exfiltrates-workflow-credentials/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1199
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
let lookback = 30d;
let compromised_actions = dynamic(["actions-cool/issues-helper","actions-cool/maintain-one-comment"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(GitHubAuditLog_CL
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
  | where Action_s has_any ("workflows.completed_workflow_run","workflows.created_workflow_run","workflows.prepared_workflow_job")
  | where RawData_s has_any (compromised_actions) or AdditionalFields_s has_any (compromised_actions)
  | project TimeGenerated, Actor_s, Repository_s, Action_s, RawData_s),
(GitHubRepoLogs
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
  | where AdditionalFields has_any (compromised_actions)
  | project TimeGenerated, Actor=tostring(AdditionalFields.actor), Repo=tostring(AdditionalFields.repository), Workflow=tostring(AdditionalFields.workflow), Reference=tostring(AdditionalFields.action_ref))
| order by TimeGenerated desc
// NOTE: replace GitHubAuditLog_CL / GitHubRepoLogs with the actual custom-log table name in your tenant — common via the GitHub data connector for Sentinel.
source:github (@workflow.uses:(actions-cool/issues-helper* OR actions-cool/maintain-one-comment*) OR @repository.workflow.uses:(actions-cool/issues-helper* OR actions-cool/maintain-one-comment*) OR @evt.name:workflows.* @rawJSON:(*actions-cool/issues-helper* OR *actions-cool/maintain-one-comment*))
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Changes.user) as user values(All_Changes.object) as workflow from datamodel=Change.All_Changes where All_Changes.object_category="file" AND All_Changes.object_path="*.github/workflows/*" AND (All_Changes.change_type="modification" OR All_Changes.change_type="created") by All_Changes.src All_Changes.object_path | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Changes)` | append [search index=github_audit OR sourcetype=github:* ("actions-cool/issues-helper" OR "actions-cool/maintain-one-comment") | stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime by repo workflow actor action_ref] | search (workflow="*actions-cool/issues-helper*" OR workflow="*actions-cool/maintain-one-comment*" OR action_ref="*actions-cool/issues-helper*" OR action_ref="*actions-cool/maintain-one-comment*")
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Changes.user) as user values(All_Changes.object) as workflow from datamodel=Change.All_Changes where All_Changes.object_category="file" AND All_Changes.object_path="*.github/workflows/*" AND (All_Changes.change_type="modification" OR All_Changes.change_type="created") by All_Changes.src All_Changes.object_path | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Changes)` | append [search index=github_audit OR sourcetype=github:* ("actions-cool/issues-helper" OR "actions-cool/maintain-one-comment") | stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime by repo workflow actor action_ref] | search (workflow="*actions-cool/issues-helper*" OR workflow="*actions-cool/maintain-one-comment*" OR action_ref="*actions-cool/issues-helper*" OR action_ref="*actions-cool/maintain-one-comment*")
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.

DeviceNetworkEvents

Active Supply Chain Attack: Malicious node-ipc Versions Published to npm

StepSecurity
2026-05-19 13 use cases 4 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Active Supply Chain Attack: Malicious node-ipc Versions Published to npm StepSecurity has detected multiple malicious releases of the popular node-ipc npm package. Three versions are currently known to be compromised, containing an obfuscated payload designed to steal cloud credentials, SSH keys, and CI/CD secrets. Our team is actively analyzing the attack, and this post will be updated as our investigation progresses

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Active Supply Chain Attack: Malicious node-ipc Versions Published to npm
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Compromised node-ipc.cjs bundle write (~117KB) under node_modules · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] node-ipc C2 callback to sh.azurestaticprovider.net (May 2026 npm supply-chain) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains · DNS tunneling / TXT-heavy domain queries
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Node.js process bulk-reading cloud & SCM credential files in single session · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
[LLM] node-ipc C2 callback to sh.azurestaticprovider.net (May 2026 npm supply-chain) Command & Control High
Detects any DNS lookup or outbound network connection to sh.azurestaticprovider.net, the credential-exfiltration C2 used by the malicious node-ipc versions 9.1.6 / 9.2.3 / 12.0.1 published 2026-05-14. The domain is a typosquat of azurestaticapps.net and has no legitimate business use — first sighting is incident-level signal. Rationale: Anchored on the literal C2 domain sh.azurestaticprovider.net pulled from the article's deobfuscated payload config (the 'r' field of the _0x501a65 attack config object). Domain typosquats Azure infrastructure and has no benign use — single-hit alerting tier is appropriate. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/node-ipc-npm-supply-chain-attack • https://www.npmjs.com/package/node-ipc
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1041 T1568
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
// node-ipc supply-chain C2: any host contacting sh.azurestaticprovider.net
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has "azurestaticprovider.net" or RemoteUrl =~ "sh.azurestaticprovider.net"
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"     // exclude machine-account noise
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
// node-ipc supply-chain C2 — union across DNS + CEF/firewall + ASIM tables
let SuspectDomain = "azurestaticprovider.net";
let StartTime = ago(30d);
union isfuzzy=true
  (DnsEvents
     | where TimeGenerated > StartTime
     | where Name has SuspectDomain
     | project TimeGenerated, Source = "DnsEvents", Host = Computer, ClientIP, QueriedName = Name, QueryType),
  (CommonSecurityLog
     | where TimeGenerated > StartTime
     | where DestinationHostName has SuspectDomain or RequestURL has SuspectDomain
     | project TimeGenerated, Source = "CommonSecurityLog", Host = SourceHostName, SrcIP = SourceIP, DstHost = DestinationHostName, DstIP = DestinationIP, URL = RequestURL),
  (ImNetworkSession
     | where TimeGenerated > StartTime
     | where DstHostname has SuspectDomain or DstDomain has SuspectDomain or Url has SuspectDomain
     | project TimeGenerated, Source = "ImNetworkSession", Host = SrcHostname, SrcIP = SrcIpAddr, DstHost = DstHostname, DstIP = DstIpAddr, URL = Url),
  (ImDnsActivity
     | where TimeGenerated > StartTime
     | where DnsQuery has SuspectDomain or DnsQueryName has SuspectDomain
     | project TimeGenerated, Source = "ImDnsActivity", Host = SrcHostname, SrcIP = SrcIpAddr, QueriedName = DnsQuery)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Compromised node-ipc.cjs bundle write (~117KB) under node_modules Installation High
Detects file-write events targeting `node_modules/node-ipc/node-ipc.cjs` whose payload exceeds 80KB after 2026-05-14, indicating installation of the malicious versions 9.1.6 / 9.2.3 / 12.0.1. The clean 12.0.0 bundle was ~37KB / 1269 lines; the trojanised bundle is ~117KB / 1271 lines with an 80KB obfuscated IIFE appended after the final module.exports. Rationale: Anchored on the exact file path (`node_modules/node-ipc/node-ipc.cjs`) and size delta (37KB clean → 117KB compromised, +80KB IIFE) called out in the article's diff block. The publication-date floor (2026-05-14) eliminates legitimate historical writes; the file-size predicate eliminates any future legitimate node-ipc release that doesn't add a comparable bundle. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/node-ipc-npm-supply-chain-attack • https://www.npmjs.com/package/node-ipc?activeTab=versions
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
// Malicious node-ipc bundle write — anomalous .cjs size under node_modules
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > datetime(2026-05-14T00:00:00Z)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where FolderPath has @"\node_modules\node-ipc\" or FolderPath has "/node_modules/node-ipc/"
| where FileName =~ "node-ipc.cjs"
| where FileSize > 80000     // clean ~37KB; trojanised ~117KB (80KB IIFE injected)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, FileSize, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
// Malicious node-ipc bundle write (ASIM file event)
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > datetime(2026-05-14T00:00:00Z)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFilePath has @"\node_modules\node-ipc\" or TargetFilePath has "/node_modules/node-ipc/"
| where TargetFileName =~ "node-ipc.cjs"
| where TargetFileSize > 80000   // clean ~37KB; trojanised ~117KB
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName,
          TargetFileSize, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Node.js process bulk-reading cloud & SCM credential files in single session Actions on Objectives Medium
Hunts for a single node process that opens >=3 distinct categories of credential artifacts (AWS, SSH, Kubernetes, Azure, GCP, GitHub CLI, Terraform, Docker, npm, Claude / Kiro IDE, shell history) within a single process lifetime. The compromised node-ipc payload harvests over 90 categories of secrets on require() — a fan-out pattern that no legitimate node tool produces in a single session. Rationale: The article enumerates 90+ credential categories the payload sweeps — AWS, Azure, GCP, SSH, Kubernetes, GitHub CLI, Claude AI, Kiro IDE, Terraform state, shell history. Mass fan-out from a single node PID is a behaviour pattern no legitimate dev tool exhibits in a single session. Sigma omitted because the detection requires aggregation across multiple file-open events keyed by process ID. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/node-ipc-npm-supply-chain-attack
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1555 T1083 T1530
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem

    @"\.claude\", @"\.kiro\",
    @"\.bash_history", @"\.zsh_history", @"\.psql_history",

| order by LastSeen desc
// node process touching multiple credential-store paths in one session (ASIM file event)
